experiments.title: Liquidity beta — sensitivity to aggregate liquidity innovations (Pastor-Stambaugh)
experiments.hypothesis: Stocks whose returns are more sensitive to fluctuations in aggregate market liquidity earn higher average returns; high-sensitivity stocks beat low-sensitivity stocks by 7.5% per year (1966-1999) adjusted for market, size, value and momentum.

literature_intake.source: Pastor & Stambaugh, Journal of Political Economy 111 (2003) 642-685
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Stocks whose returns are more sensitive to fluctuations in aggregate market liquidity earn higher average returns; high-sensitivity stocks beat low-sensitivity stocks by 7.5% per year (1966-1999) adjusted for market, size, value and momentum.

Preregistration should report correlation with Harvest #4 IH02 aggregate-volatility beta sorts; a pass that merely re-measures the Amihud level or volatility beta is not a new finding.

experiments.title: Net share issuance — issuers underperform, repurchasers outperform (Pontiff-Woodgate)
experiments.hypothesis: Post-1970, share issuance strongly predicts cross-sectional returns: firms that grow their split-adjusted share count underperform and firms that shrink it outperform.

literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Post-1970, share issuance strongly predicts cross-sectional returns: firms that grow their split-adjusted share count underperform and firms that shrink it outperform.

experiments.title: Accrual anomaly (Sloan) — cash-backed earnings beat accrual-heavy earnings
experiments.hypothesis: The lowest-accrual decile outperformed the highest-accrual decile by ~10.4 pp per year (~9.4 pp size-adjusted, 1962-1991): prices fixate on earnings and underweight the lower persistence of the accrual component relative to cash flow.

literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: The lowest-accrual decile outperformed the highest-accrual decile by ~10.4 pp per year (~9.4 pp size-adjusted, 1962-1991): prices fixate on earnings and underweight the lower persistence of the accrual component relative to cash flow.

experiments.title: Earnings announcement premium — prices rise around scheduled announcement dates (Frazzini-Lamont)
experiments.hypothesis: Stocks expected to announce earnings in a month earn a premium over stocks not expected to announce (~61 bp/month, ~7%/yr, t>5; premium lasts ~20 days), regardless of the news content.

literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Stocks expected to announce earnings in a month earn a premium over stocks not expected to announce (~61 bp/month, ~7%/yr, t>5; premium lasts ~20 days), regardless of the news content.

experiments.title: Short interest — heavily shorted stocks underperform (Asquith-Pathak-Ritter)
experiments.hypothesis: High short interest portfolios generally underperform; short-sale-constrained stocks (highest short interest percentile and lowest institutional-ownership third) underperformed by 215 bp/month equal-weighted (1988-2002) but only an insignificant 39 bp/month value-weighted.

literature_intake.source: Asquith, Pathak & Ritter, Journal of Financial Economics 78 (2005) 243-276
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: High short interest portfolios generally underperform; short-sale-constrained stocks (highest short interest percentile and lowest institutional-ownership third) underperformed by 215 bp/month equal-weighted (1988-2002) but only an insignificant 39 bp/month value-weighted.

experiments.rule_spec_version: IDEA_HARVEST_SPEC_v1 intake; no rule spec yet
dependencies: FINRA/exchange published short interest (dissemination dates) and SEC EDGAR 13F institutional ownership (filed dates), plus daily price data.
experiments.next_action: Awaiting Mike selection; if picked, next step is a preregistration with a frozen gate (separate approval).
experiments.acceptance_criteria: TBD — frozen gate to be written before any run
limitations: Non-negotiable PIT rule: signal keyed to the short interest DISSEMINATION date, never the settlement date; 13F ownership keyed to filed dates.

Paper's own caveats: headline effect is equal-weighted and concentrated in a tiny constrained subset (~21 stocks/month in full CRSP); on a ~250-name large-cap universe that subset may be nearly empty and a value-weighted null is a live possibility.

Honest form is long-only avoidance/underweight of heavily shorted names; a short leg belongs only inside a long-short research design with borrow costs stated, and a daily short-side system would collide with KILLED-SHORT-SIDE-DAILY.
Dedupe PASS with form restriction flagged: no registry experiment uses positioning data.

experiments.title: Distress / failure probability — high-failure-probability stocks earn anomalously low returns (Campbell-Hilscher-Szilagyi)
experiments.hypothesis: Stocks with high failure probability estimated by a dynamic logit on accounting and market variables have delivered anomalously low returns since 1981, despite higher volatility, betas and value/small-cap loadings.

literature_intake.source: Campbell, Hilscher & Szilagyi, Journal of Finance 63 (2008) 2899-2947
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Stocks with high failure probability estimated by a dynamic logit on accounting and market variables have delivered anomalously low returns since 1981, despite higher volatility, betas and value/small-cap loadings.

experiments.title: Option-implied volatility spread — put-call parity deviations predict stock returns (Cremers-Weinbaum)
experiments.hypothesis: Stocks with relatively expensive calls outperform stocks with relatively expensive puts by 50 bp per week, where expensiveness is the call-minus-put implied-volatility spread on matched strike/expiry option pairs.

literature_intake.source: Cremers & Weinbaum, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 45 (2010) 335-367

literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Stocks with relatively expensive calls outperform stocks with relatively expensive puts by 50 bp per week, where expensiveness is the call-minus-put implied-volatility spread on matched strike/expiry option pairs.
